notes: Kent State CS department page https://www.kent.edu/cs/academic-dishonesty (fetched as v2-kent-state-cs-dishonesty.txt) is a policy on collaboration in programming assignments and has no AI or GAI text, so it was not collected. Computing therefore counts as none-found, though the page does state the department's cooperation rules. The Kent news item about the policy revision (kent.edu/today/news/adding-ai-cheating-and-plagiarism-policy) is a news article and was not collected. The CTL faculty AI pages (kent.edu/ai/faculty) return 'Access denied'; search snippets say the CTL offers model syllabus language for AI prohibited / permitted / integrated, but the text was not retrieved. Reconciliation: non-AI hearing-panel mechanics (panel composition, annual training, eligibility to sit, recordings) found only by B were dropped; sanction, hearing and appeal rules that apply to GAI misuse via the cheating definition were kept.

documents.unit: University Policy Register (Office of General Counsel / Provost)
documents.title: 3342-3-01.8 Administrative policy regarding student cheating and plagiarism
documents.date_or_term: current (accessed 2026-10-25); revised to add generative AI
documents.stance_why: Both coders: GAI is cheating on exams ('except as expressly permitted by the instructor in the syllabus, examination, test, or quiz') and on assigned coursework ('except as expressly permitted by the instructor in the syllabus, or applicable assignment'). AI is barred by default and allowed only where the instructor permits, and the document sets that default itself with no tiers, so restrict rather than delegates.
documents.summary: Kent State's administrative policy on student cheating and plagiarism, revised to add generative AI. GAI is defined, barred on exams and coursework unless the instructor expressly permits it, and added to the cheating and plagiarism definitions, with the general sanction, appeal and hearing procedures applying.

units.why: The purpose clause says academic work follows "standards set by faculty members, departments, schools and colleges", so standards are set below the university level; this is a general principle placing authority with instructors and units, which fits P04 (who decides) better than P56, since it is not an AI-specific framework.
units.resolution_why: Matched (A0, B0). Both code the purpose clause that students work to 'standards set by faculty members, departments, schools and colleges' as P04, student, general, must. B added a normalized policy that stays within the passage; kept it.

units.frag_start: Students enrolled in the university
units.policy: Students perform their academic work according to standards set by faculty members, departments, schools and colleges.

units.why: States that "cheating and plagiarism constitute fraudulent misrepresentation for which no credit can be given" and sanctions "will be applied"; it is the general rationale for treating improper work (which includes GAI misuse) as misconduct, so P36.
units.resolution_why: Matched (A9, B1). Both: P36, when-misuse, informs. A said actor all and unit_stance restrict; B said student and neutral. The sentence tells students that cheating gets no credit and sanctions, but it is a statement of consequence, not a restriction on AI itself (the sentence does not mention GAI), so neutral; the purpose clause is addressed to enrolled students, so student. Policy text rewritten to quote the source only.
units.anchor: no credit can be given and for which appropriate sanctions are warranted
units.frag_start: Students enrolled in the university
units.policy: Cheating and plagiarism constitute fraudulent misrepresentation for which no credit can be given and for which appropriate sanctions are warranted and will be applied.

units.why: Defines cheating to include "content generated by internet-based generative artificial intelligence programs (GAI), in examinations, tests and quizzes" unless the instructor permits it; this is an exam ban with an instructor-permission exception, so P22 (exam ban) rather than P06 (fallback), and it also classifies it as cheating.
units.resolution_why: Matched (A1, B2). Both: P22, student, during-assessment, must-not, restrict. Source: 'content generated by ... (GAI), in examinations, tests and quizzes, except as expressly permitted'. Kept B's policy, which carries the exception.

units.frag_start: Using notes, textbooks or other information, or content
units.policy: Using content generated by internet-based generative artificial intelligence programs (GAI) in examinations, tests and quizzes is cheating, except as expressly permitted by the instructor in the syllabus, examination, test, or quiz.

units.why: The exception "except as expressly permitted by the instructor in the syllabus, examination, test, or quiz" lets each instructor decide whether GAI is allowed on exams, so P04 (instructor sets the rule) is assigned; the exam ban itself is coded separately under P22.
units.resolution_why: Matched (A2, B3). Both: P04, instructor, may, permit. Phase differed: A during-assessment, B before-course. The source says permission is given 'in the syllabus, examination, test, or quiz', that is, it is a communicated expectation, not course design or the exam act itself, so course-start (the same phase A gave the coursework counterpart).

units.frag_start: Using notes, textbooks or other information, or content
units.policy: The instructor may expressly permit GAI use in an examination, test or quiz in the syllabus or in the examination, test or quiz itself.

units.why: The coursework ban holds "except as expressly permitted by the instructor in the syllabus, or applicable assignment", so the instructor or assignment sets whether GAI is allowed. This is per-instructor and per-assignment authority, P04. P06 (silent syllabus) is a second fit, but this unit is about who permits.
units.resolution_why: Only coder A coded this. Source: 'Using GAI to generate content in satisfaction of assigned coursework, except as expressly permitted by the instructor in the syllabus, or applicable assignment'. This mirrors the exam permission unit and is a distinct rule (instructor may permit GAI on coursework), so kept as P04 course-start may.

units.why: "Using GAI to generate content in satisfaction of assigned coursework" is defined as cheating unless the instructor expressly permits it, i.e. students may not have AI produce the work they submit: P19, not P22 because it concerns coursework not exams.
units.resolution_why: Matched (A3, B4). Both P19, student, during-work, must-not. A said prohibit, B restrict. The prohibition carries the clause 'except as expressly permitted by the instructor', so it is a default ban with an exception: restrict. Topics follow A, since the passage says 'content', not code; B's code-generation tag is dropped.

units.frag_start: Using GAI to generate content in satisfaction

units.why: The phrase "except as expressly permitted" means AI is banned unless the instructor says otherwise; the default when the syllabus is silent is prohibition. This fallback rule is P06; P01 is close but the document pairs the default with a required express permission.
units.resolution_why: Matched (A5, B5). Both P06 (the default when the syllabus does not permit). A: student, during-work, must-not; B: all, course-start, must. The rule binds students and applies when the work is done and no permission was given, so student, during-work, must-not, restrict. Policy rewritten to match the source's wording ('is cheating').

units.why: Cheating includes "Having another person, or GAI, take one's place for any academic performance without the specific knowledge and permission of the instructor"; AI substituting for the student is forbidden unless the instructor knowingly permits, which is a ban on AI producing the submitted performance, P19.
units.resolution_why: Matched (A7, B7). Both P19, student, during-work, must-not. A prohibit, B restrict. The source ends 'without the specific knowledge and permission of the instructor', so restrict.

units.why: The plagiarism definition names GAI as a source: taking and presenting "the ideas or words of another (e.g. person, persons, or GAI)" as one's own is plagiarism. It treats GAI like an outside source under existing plagiarism rules, so P45; P36 covers classification as misconduct but this unit is about the source analogy.
units.resolution_why: Matched (A8, B8). Both P45, student/general. A: informs; B: must-not. The passage is a definition of 'plagiarize' that names GAI alongside persons; the prohibition is in the policy's other parts, so the passage informs. Unit stance restrict (GAI treated like another author who must be credited).

units.frag_start: "Plagiarize" means to take and present
units.frag_end: proper credit to the source of the ideas, words, or works.
units.policy: Plagiarize means to take and present as one's own a material portion of the ideas or words of another (e.g. person, persons, or GAI) without full and proper credit.
